messages.subject: Changing Class Of Multiple Columns
parts:
I am currently importing a df that contains dates/times. The problem
is that the dates are being imported into R as factors. I would like
to change the class of multiple columns to the POSIXct class. I have
tried using the colwise function as part of the plyr package with no
luck and was hoping someone could point me in the right direction.

Example Code1:
sample = read.table(sample.txt,header=TRUE)
class(sample[,4])
ddply(sample,.(Object,WorkOrder),colwise(as.POSIXct,.
(Accession_Oligos,QC_Oligo_Pool,Make_Pool_Trough)),.progress="text")
class(sample[,4])

Example Code 2:
as_Date = function(x) as.POSIXct(x)
ddply(sample,.(Object,WorkOrder),colwise(as_Date,.
(Accession_Oligos,QC_Oligo_Pool,Make_Pool_Trough)),.progress="text")
class(sample[,4])

messages.author: 5a1b5a9591c118ef
messages.subject: Re: Changing Class Of Multiple Columns
parts:
Hi,

I haven't tried your data but here are two suggestions,

1- read.table has two arguments that could help you with the import:
colClasses and stringsAsFactors.

2- To apply a function to specific columns of a data.frame, I use the following,

ize = function (d, columns = names(d), izer = as.POSIXct, ...)
{
d[columns] = lapply(d[columns], izer, ...)
d
}

HTH,

baptiste

parts:
if you know which columns (names or index) have to be changed, just
pass it to ize() as the columns argument. I you don't know, then
you'll probably have to do some regular expression search on the first
few lines to figure it out.

HTH,

baptiste
